Either way you should read the wiki page for anarchocapitalism on mises wiki and see if that makes you happy with the term.

I prefer the term free-market anarchist. I think the problem is that lefty anarchists, seeing the current statist-distorted markets, equate them with capitalism. The term capitalism is just too muddled to be useful for us at this point. It makes sense, depending on how one defines capitalism.

Well I rather like the dictionary definition, an economic system where the means of production are in private hands and operated for profit. But that clearly isn't how capitalism is always used. That's why it's a problematic term, although maybe rehabilitatable.

I think it's the fault of rent seeking, regulatory capture, our guild ridden economic system, and etc. If we removed the political means of wealth allocation while preserving private property, people would only be able to legitimately get things via voluntary trade. Of course, I'll always admit I could be wrong.

And the problems with capitalism today have always existed since what we know as capitalism first existed, and even before.

They're both contradictory.

Anarchy is anarchy. It comes in all flavors. That's its nature when controllers are fukt.

Anarcho-Capitalism is kind of a redundancy, while Anarcho-Communism is an oxymoron.

Capitalism means without government interference in commerce, while anarchy means "without rulers". Slightly different, but not by much.

Communism is regulated economy with central planners (rulers). You can't be communist and anarchist at the same time. It literally means "Ruler-less with Rulers"

INGREDIENTS

2 1/4 cups all-purpose flour 1/2 teaspoon baking soda 1 cup (2 sticks) unsalted butter, room temperature 1/2 cup granulated sugar 1 cup packed light-brown sugar 1 teaspoon salt 2 teaspoons pure vanilla extract 2 large eggs 2 cups (about 12 ounces) semisweet and/or milk chocolate chips

DIRECTIONS

Preheat oven to 350 degrees. In a small bowl, whisk together the flour and baking soda; set aside. In the bowl of an electric mixer fitted with the paddle attachment, combine the butter with both sugars; beat on medium speed until light and fluffy. Reduce speed to low; add the salt, vanilla, and eggs. Beat until well mixed, about 1 minute. Add flour mixture; mix until just combined. Stir in the chocolate chips. Drop heaping tablespoon-size balls of dough about 2 inches apart on baking sheets lined with parchment paper. Bake until cookies are golden around the edges, but still soft in the center, 8 to 10 minutes. Remove from oven, and let cool on baking sheet 1 to 2 minutes. Transfer to a wire rack, and let cool completely. Store cookies in an airtight container at room temperature up to 1 week.
